modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Export and hash the selected record and adjacent metadata, bind a valid reservation, obtain final exact-record approval, issue one delete, verify only that ID is absent and retain the irreversible audit.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents an argument-free or full-log deletion and requires record-specific preservation and proof.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: SEL clear does not validate single-record delete; read-only evidence cannot claim delete PASS.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Deletion may be irreversible and remove forensic/compliance evidence; some firmware may not support it.

project_override_considerations: A vendor API is equivalent only if it deletes exactly one identified record with authorization and preserved audit; full-log erase is never an override for this case.
expected_evidence: Immutable target record and surrounding metadata

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master names a single-entry delete but supplies no request data and clears the entire evidence baseline beforehand; transport-only Criteria cannot identify what was deleted. DeepSeek confirms no executable bytes are available.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing record selector/reservation and delete-support semantics define the core destructive action, not merely project expected values, so execution cannot be safely packaged.

review_improvement: Separates single-entry deletion from full clear and establishes exact irreversible evidence and authorization boundaries.
independent_technical_reasoning: A bare destructive command cannot prove or constrain target identity. Because deletion may permanently remove forensic evidence, exact record/reservation semantics must be decided before the case can leave BLOCKED.
